checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated streamlined body with notably extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is very long and cylindrical/streamlined, fitting the general description of an elongated marine/freshwater fish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small silvery scales with bluish-green dorsal coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays a distinct pattern of light spots on a darker greenish/brown background (reticulated or spotted), which is characteristic of Northern Pike. Barracouta typically have uniform silvery sides with a blue-green back and no such prominent spotting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Separated dorsal fins; first dorsal spiny, second dorsal soft-rayed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only one dorsal fin is clearly visible, located far back on the body near the tail. Barracouta have two separated dorsal fins further forward. This anatomy matches Esox (Pike).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anal fin similar to second dorsal.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anal fin is visible and positioned opposite the single rear dorsal fin, consistent with the visible anatomy (though inconsistent with the target class).
The caudal fin (tail) appears rounded or slightly truncate, not deeply forked as required for Barracouta.
